new_statements.quote: Stress in Gurr-goni is to a large degree grammatically predictable: it is placed on the first syllable of the root. (Primary stress is shown here by an acute accent placed before the stressed syllable.) Where the root takes prefixes, the first syllable of the prefix, or series of prefixes, takes secondary stress ... In compound stems, formed of two or more roots, the first syllable of the first root may receive primary stress, while the first syllable of the second root takes secondary stress. This is so both for (many) reduplicated forms, and for other compounds ... Often, however, compound forms (but not reduplicated forms), have the primary stress on the first syllable of the second root, and secondary stress on the first.
new_statements.citation: Green, Rebecca. 1995. A grammar of Gurr-goni (North Central Arnhem Land). PhD thesis, Australian National University.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the first syllable of the root (root-initial, morphologically determined); in unprefixed words this is word-initial. Prefix strings carry secondary stress on their first syllable. In compounds and reduplications primary stress is on the first root and secondary on the second, though lexicalised compounds often reverse this.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on the first syllable of the prefix (or prefix series); in compounds/reduplications, secondary stress on the first syllable of whichever root does not carry primary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: 69 apparent exceptions in a vocabulary of ~1200, almost all analysable as containing a frozen unstressed prefix (bV-, gV-, mV-, nu-, na-) or as old compounds; Kuninjku loans (nawaran 'python', manberg 'uplands') stress the borrowed prefix; stress shifts from monosyllabic root wu 'give' onto a preceding prefix syllable -bu-, and may shift onto the pronominal prefix before ni 'sit' in the zero-suffixed Precontemporary/Irrealis 2 tenses.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress described relative to morphological structure (root vs prefixes); examples are inflected verb and noun words in citation. Author's orthographic convention (p. 34): primary stress marked only where not obvious, i.e. not the first syllable or the first syllable after a prefix hyphen.
new_statements.identity_note: Green 1995 describes Gurr-goni (= Glottolog Guragone gura1252, ISO gge; older spelling Gungurugoni in Elwell 1977, Gurrgoni in StressTyp). Single variety; c. 1200-item vocabulary.
